note: Four workers with 32 threads and connections kept for ten minutes can hold 128 database connections, more than Postgres allows, so under evening streaming load the health check's database query fails with too many clients.

cause.title: perf: serve more parallel stream requests
cause.author: Philipp Klinger
cause.patch:
diff --git a/backend.entrypoint.sh b/backend.entrypoint.sh
@@ -24,8 +24,9 @@ case "$1" in
     # No access log: activation and reset tokens are part of request paths.
+    # HLS segments are many small requests: more threads instead of more memory per worker.
     exec gunicorn core.wsgi:application \
       --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 \
       --worker-class gthread \
-      --workers "${GUNICORN_WORKERS:-2}" \
-      --threads "${GUNICORN_THREADS:-4}" \
+      --workers "${GUNICORN_WORKERS:-4}" \
+      --threads "${GUNICORN_THREADS:-32}" \
       --timeout "${GUNICORN_TIMEOUT:-120}"
     ;;
diff --git a/core/settings.py b/core/settings.py
@@ -144,7 +144,9 @@ DATABASES = {
         "USER": os.environ.get("DB_USER", default="videoflix_user"),
         "PASSWORD": DB_PASSWORD,
         "HOST": os.environ.get("DB_HOST", default="db"),
-        "PORT": os.environ.get("DB_PORT", default=5432)
+        "PORT": os.environ.get("DB_PORT", default=5432),
+        # Reuse connections between requests instead of opening one per segment.
+        "CONN_MAX_AGE": int(os.environ.get("DB_CONN_MAX_AGE", "600")),
     }
 }
cause.body:
HLS players fetch a segment every four seconds per viewer, and eight threads
queued them during the demo. Four workers with 32 threads each, and database
connections kept between requests, avoid a new connection per segment.
